This phone\'s Bluetooth chip may keep its address when the ID changes, so a scanner nearby could still link your IDs. Rotating IDs protect less on this phone.

Renames your phone to \"Phone\" across Bluetooth connections, including headphones, cars and computers. Turn this off to restore its name. If you uninstall MeshLive first, you\'ll need to rename it in Android settings.

This renames your phone for everything: headphones, your car, your watch, PCs and Quick Share will show \"Phone\". Your name now: %1$s. Turn this option off to get it back. If you uninstall the app while it is on, the name stays \"Phone\" until you rename the phone in Android settings.

Recommended on this phone: its Bluetooth chip cannot hide the name from phones that connect.

Recommended on this phone: its Bluetooth refused to hide the name, so phones that connect can read it.
Without Private Bluetooth ID the name is readable by phones that connect. Turn it on to hide it on Android 14 and newer, or use this option on any phone.

While Private Bluetooth ID is on, phones that connect to you without being paired cannot read the name on this phone. Calls you place and streams you send still show it to the phone you connect to, and Classic Bluetooth lookups see it; this option hides it there too.
Off for now: allow Nearby devices for MeshLive in Android settings to hide the name.
Off for now: Android did not allow MeshLive to rename the phone.

Experimental. Let nearby phones help carry private calls further. Helping phones can see which phones connect and when, but can\'t hear or watch calls. Some privacy settings limit compatibility. Helping pauses below 20% battery unless charging, and in Battery Saver. Your own calls and streams take priority.

Other phones can help people reach you through up to two helping phones. They can see which phones are calling and when, but can\'t hear or watch the call. Your availability may also be shared further away. Change these choices in Settings.
Ask the other person to open MeshLive. Stay within about 10 to 30 metres. Both phones need a current MeshLive. The list updates by itself.
%1$s, %2$s. Tap to call. Touch and hold for details.

MeshLive needs more access. Allow it in Settings > Apps > MeshLive > Permissions.
Share a crash report? It lists where the app failed, its version and the phone model. It has no names, messages, keys or IDs, and you choose where to send it.

resources.string: %1$d phone settings may stop calls and video in the background
Android may pause the app in the background, which can drop calls and shared video. Allow it to run without battery restrictions.
Creates a short technical report (app version, phone model, Bluetooth support). It contains no video, sound, messages, names or keys. You choose where to send it; it is also copied.
No app can open the bug report page. Open the project page on a phone with internet.

Off by default. Adds an optional name (Settings, Your name) and a title when you go live. Names travel only inside the encrypted call, signed by your identity key; a stream title is also advertised publicly so people nearby see it before joining (shown as unconfirmed until they join). Phones without this see only your handle.
Your name is never broadcast. It is sent, encrypted, only to the people you choose under Who sees my name, and your QR code shows it. Without a name, others see a made-up name.
Optional. You choose who sees it
